If I am understanding the logic of the code below, it is trying to find both an EM chassis and an EM motherboard that have the correct chassis number.  I don't think it needs to be this complicated (I could be wrong).

We discussed with Matt that *both* the EM chassis and the EM motherboard would provide the Slot interface.

In the case of PSU properties, they are currently being stored as part of the EM motherboard info.  So you only need to find the motherboard that contains the PSU properties, and then determine if that has the correct chassis number.

```
$ busctl tree xyz.openbmc_project.EntityManager
        │ └─ /xyz/openbmc_project/inventory/system/board/Nisqually_Backplane
        │   ├─ /xyz/openbmc_project/inventory/system/board/Nisqually_Backplane/Power_Supply_Slot_0
        │   ├─ /xyz/openbmc_project/inventory/system/board/Nisqually_Backplane/Power_Supply_Slot_1
```

Someone could decide to put the PSU info in the EM chassis object instead.  So either way, we just want to find PSU info that is contained within an EM object path with the correct chassis number.

I think the logic could just be the following right?
* Find all objects that implement the IBMCFFPSInterface interface (as you are already doing)
* Find all objects that provide a "chassis number" (by implementing the Slot interface)
* Loop through "chassis number" providing objects
  * If the object has the correct chassis number
    * Loop through the IBMCFFPSInterface objects
      * If the "chassis number" object path is a parent of the PS object path
        * This PS belongs in the correct chassis
        * Note: Keep looping to find more matching PS objects

You can check if a "chassis number" object is a parent of a PS object by checking if the PS object path starts with the "chassis number" object path.

For example:
`/xyz/openbmc_project/inventory/system/board/Nisqually_Backplane/Power_Supply_Slot_0`
starts with
`/xyz/openbmc_project/inventory/system/board/Nisqually_Backplane`

I would recommend doing the 'starts with' test rather that assuming the PSU info is exactly one node below the parent.  That would provide protection in case EM changed their object path design and the PSU info was 2 or 3 levels below the parent.

I think this algorithm below will add all the PSUs in the system to every chassis.

Faisal and I talked offline about using the following algorithm instead:
```
* Get chassis number (slot number) for chassis path from PIM (same as current code)
* Get all D-Bus paths that implement CFFPS interface (e.g. the PSU D-Bus paths)
* Loop through PSU D-Bus paths
  * Get parent D-Bus path
  * Get chassis number (slot number) for parent D-Bus path
  * If chassis number matches
    * Get properties of PSU and add to current C++ Chassis object
```
